Maya, in her early thirties, short black hair in a pixie cut, a thin scar on her left eyebrow, wears a heather-grey sweater and a midnight-blue coat. In the early evening she reads a letter in the living room of her small apartment. Then she sets the letter on the table. So she stands up, still in the living room, and tidies the papers by the window.

The next day.
After that, in the kitchen, at 10 a.m., Maya opens the fridge. In the kitchen, she sets a cup on the counter. Then she pours hot water. She waits in a silence. She thinks of the beach. Suddenly Luca comes in, in his early forties, a short red beard, a bottle-green sweater, a beige canvas bag, a white paint stain on the sleeve. He says, "We should go to the beach." Maya smiles at him and closes the fridge.

Later, at the station, Maya finds Luca by the departures board. They compare their tickets. Luca hands her an envelope.

At nightfall, in the café across the street, they sit down by the window. Maya opens the envelope. Then she slips it into the pocket of her midnight-blue coat.
